task_objective: Use safe host and connection tests to investigate why a USB drive is detected on one computer but not another.
constraints: Preserve the drive's existing data: do not format, initialize, repartition or destructively repair it as an initial detection test. Read-only diagnosis complies without an explicit backup warning; any later modifying repair needs a recoverable copy.

rius.description: Test the failing computer's USB connection path with at least one controlled comparison, such as a known-working port or cable, bypassing a hub, or checking an appropriate power supply when the drive requires one.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Test the failing computer's USB connection path with at least one controlled comparison, such as a known-working port or cable, bypassing a hub, or checking an appropriate power supply when the drive requires one.

rius.rationale: Tests a local connection or power problem through alternative first checks rather than requiring every interface test.

rius.description: Check whether the failing computer recognizes the drive at the device or disk level, distinguishing complete non-detection from a recognized disk that lacks a usable mounted volume.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.

rius.rationale: Distinguishes hardware detection from a missing mounted volume, but other sound connection or host tests can still make progress without this explicit layer check; no single diagnostic branch is established as decisive.

rius.description: Investigate at least one host-specific explanation using the working computer as a reference, such as USB/driver status, access policy, filesystem compatibility or volume mounting.
